A standard Product Requirements Document (PRD) template helps align product, design, and engineering teams by outlining what to build and why. You can find ready-to-use layouts via the [Atlassian Confluence PRD Template](https://www.atlassian.com/software/confluence/templates/product-requirements) or browse various structures on the [Notion PRD Marketplace](https://www.notion.com/templates/category/product-requirements-doc).

### Core PRD Template Structure

- **Metadata & Overview** 
	- Product Name & Version
	- Document Owner / Author
	- Target Release Date & Status
	- Core Team & Stakeholders
- **Problem Statement & Objectives** 
	- Background / Why build this
	- Business & Product Goals
	- Measurable Success Metrics (KPIs)
- **Target Audience & Scope** 
	- User Personas & Target Segments
	- User Stories & Use Cases
	- In-Scope vs. Out-of-Scope Items
- **Functional & Technical Requirements** 
	- Core Features & Priority Levels
	- Acceptance Criteria
	- Technical & System Constraints
	- Assumptions & Dependencies
- **Design & Support** 
	- UX / UI Mockups & Flows
	- Open Questions & Risks

If you'd like, let me know:

- What **type of product** you are building (mobile app, B2B SaaS, hardware, etc.)
- Which **specific section** you need help writing out

I can draft a customized template section or full outline for you.
